title: A right, but not an obligation

cues.text: Forget factories for two minutes. Somebody gives Nell a voucher. It says: you may buy this bicycle for forty pounds, on any day you like. It never expires. And it never forces you to buy anything.
Question. Is the voucher worth anything before she uses it?
Of course it is. Somebody would buy it off her. It gives her a right she would not otherwise have, and it never obliges her to do anything at all.
And here is the point. The moment she uses it, the voucher is gone. She has a bicycle instead. She cannot use it again, and she cannot sell it on.
The voucher is the chance to build.
The forty pounds is the sunk cost — the money she cannot get back.
And the bicycle is all the revenue the factory will ever earn.
intrinsic value. What using the chance right now would give you.
holding premium. What the waiting itself is worth.
Which gives the rule, in one line. Use the chance when the holding premium has fallen to zero. Not before.
Before that point, waiting is still worth something, and building throws it away for nothing.
worth something before it is used
